defining_records.title: RETRIEVAL FORMATION THEORY The Conditions of Disciplinary Emergence in Automated Knowledge Infrastructure

captures.description: 'Retrieval Formation Theory, pioneered by theorist Lee Sharks, is a conceptual framework exploring how meaning, context, and information are retrieved, shaped, and synthesized by AI-mediated platforms and large language models (LLMs).' Core Concepts: The AI Summarizer Layer ('coherent, cross-referenced, and durably published bodies of work dictate what AI systems identify and report as objective knowledge'), Semantic Physics. leesharks.com 'Lee Sharks — Poet, Independent Scholar, Archive Builder' first organic. Google Scholar shows 'Semantic Physics: The Inward Turn, Competing...' Cited by 5. High-value scholarly-surface capture.

captures.description: RETRIEVAL FORMATION THEORY: at the bare term the AI Overview gives RFT as the study of the conditions under which a body of work 'becomes legible, discoverable, and reproducible through automated knowledge infrastructures', with #553's definition of a retrieval formation ('the configuration of terminological, citational, institutional, and substrate conditions') and the meaning layer of #581, naming no author. Three of its six sources are memory-retrieval papers, from which it builds a cognitive-psychology 'retrieval formation' to set RFT apart from.
